sections.h2: How do I reach the Stokes County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Walk in at 1014 Main Street, Danbury, ZIP 27016, or write to P.O. Box 67. The listed lines are (336) 593-2414 for the office and (336) 593-9360 for fax.

Stokes County Register of Deeds service windows
ServiceWeekday hours listed by the county
General office8:30 to 5:00
Recording documents8:30 to 4:45
Marriage license applicationsUntil 4:30

The recording window closes a quarter hour before the office does, so a deed delivered at ten to five likely waits until the next business day.

sections.h2: What does this office do in a home sale?
sections.html:
The register keeps, indexes and preserves the county's land and vital records. Three filings tend to appear in a Stokes County sale: the seller's deed, the buyer's deed of trust if there is a loan, and the release of the seller's old loan.

Stokes County itself is young compared to its neighbor. It was split off in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry County, which means a title chain for land near the line may run into Surry's books, and those go back to 1771.

sections.h2: Does a Stokes County deed need tax clearance first?
sections.html:
It does. Tax Administration says every deed offered for recording must include its certification that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property being transferred, citing G.S. 161-31.

An unpaid bill therefore holds the deed back. The tax office shares the building and street address, so the errand is short, and it keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00.

sections.h2: What does a Danbury filing cost?
sections.html:
Statute sets the amounts: $26.00 buys a standard instrument of 15 pages, and each page beyond adds $4.00. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at $64.00 for 35 pages. Filing a loan release is free.

Add $25.00 if a document misses the formatting rules and $10.00 for each extra instrument in one filing. The statute calls the schedule complete and exclusive, due up front. The seller's deed tax is separate and is paid here too.

sections.h2: Why does fast filing help both sides?
sections.html:
North Carolina ranks competing claims by the order of registration. Until a deed is registered where the property sits, it does not defeat lien creditors or paying buyers (G.S. 47-18).

The buyer wants priority. The seller wants a clean break, because claims against the buyer that arise afterward cannot reach back. Keep a copy showing the date and time of filing.

sections.h2: Do installment land contracts get recorded at Danbury?
sections.html:
They should. Chapter 47H reaches deals where the seller holds title to a home of up to four units and the buyer pays at least five installments. Either the contract or a memorandum must be filed within five business days of signing, and the buyer has until midnight of the third business day to cancel.

  • A default notice must leave a cure period of at least 30 days.
  • Late charges stop at 4% and start only after 15 days.

If you sold this way years ago, check that the memorandum is indexed in Danbury.

sections.h2: What can a Stokes County seller do before recording day?
sections.html:
Work through this list with your closing attorney.

  • Confirm the parcel with the county GIS site and the tax website's property record card.
  • Obtain the tax certification from the office down the hall.
  • Work out the deed tax from the sale price using the $1.00 per $500.00 formula.
  • Check that any old mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Arrive before 4:45 on a weekday.

For title questions about an inherited or vacant house, speak with a North Carolina attorney, and call the register about document form.

sections.h2: Which other Stokes County offices share the Danbury address?
sections.html:
The Administration Building at 1014 Main Street houses more than one office a seller will visit. Tax Administration is there, along with Planning and Inspections at (336) 593-2444, and the Finance Department, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 20.

  • Planning and Inspections keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and asks that permit applications arrive by 4:30 in the afternoon to be processed the same day.
  • The Finance Department lists (336) 914-9188.
  • The Register of Deeds uses (336) 593-2414.

One trip to Danbury can therefore cover the tax certification, a permit question and the recording itself.

sections.h2: What planning documents should a Stokes County seller know about?
sections.html:
The planning page links the county's 2035 Vision Plan, titled Moving Together, along with planning board materials for meetings held during 2026. It also notes that a regional transportation organization based in Winston-Salem published a draft 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan for public comment through September 15, 2025.

None of that changes how a deed is recorded, but a buyer evaluating a rural parcel may ask what is planned nearby. Planning and Inspections can answer zoning and code enforcement questions at (336) 593-2444.

sections.h2: What changes when the owner has died?
sections.html:
Small estates can skip full administration. Once 30 days have passed, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk serving the decedent's home county, provided personal property net of liens is under $20,000 (or under $30,000 for a spouse who is the only heir). The affidavit must describe every tract of land owned.

Larger estates take the longer route. Either way, the deed that finally conveys the house is filed in Danbury with the tax certification, so bring the court papers.

sections.h2: What happens to a recorded deed of trust in a foreclosure?
sections.html:
A lender or trustee starts by filing a notice of hearing with the clerk of superior court. The clerk has to find a valid debt, a default and a right to foreclose. An owner can appeal that finding in 10 days by posting a bond of 1% of principal unless the judge lowers it.

After the sale is reported, upset bids must top the last one by 5% or $750 added, whichever is greater, with a deposit. A borrower who sells before the hearing usually keeps more equity, and the payoff ends with a release filed in Danbury.

sections.h2: What does the Stokes County tax calendar mean for a deed?
sections.html:
Stokes bills come due by January 5, with interest from January 6. The tax certification a deed needs reflects what the county's books show owed on the parcel at that moment, so a house sold in autumn, after bills go out, usually has an open current-year balance.

Plan to settle it at the closing table. Tax Administration can quote a figure, and the tax website lists property record cards and land and home values that confirm what the county has on file for your parcel.

sections.h2: Which towns and school system sit behind a Stokes County address?
sections.html:
The county website links to the town sites for Danbury, King and Walnut Cove, and to the Stokes County school system. A buyer comparing houses will often start there, then ask the register's office only about the paper side of the transfer.

Where a house sits matters for permits and utilities, but the deed still records at Danbury whatever town the parcel lies in. Use the county GIS site to confirm which jurisdiction a parcel falls under before you advertise it.

faqs.q: What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds recording hours?
faqs.a: The county lists recording from 8:30 to 4:45 on weekdays, with the general office open 8:30 to 5:00.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Stokes County deeds?
faqs.a: P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

faqs.q: Does a Stokes deed need tax clearance first?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property before the deed is offered for recording.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax in Danbury?
faqs.a: The seller, at the register's window before recording, at one dollar per $500.00 of price with any remainder counted as another block.

faqs.q: Is a loan release free to record in Danbury?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no fee for filing a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.
